games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling Combination Tag
games.significance: The starting bell: singles, tags and five-on-five elimination contests.
games.history: The original Human Entertainment Fire Pro game established a Japanese wrestling series built around fictionalized versions of real wrestlers.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling 2nd Bout
games.significance: Expands the foundation laid by Combination Tag.
games.history: A PC Engine follow-up with more wrestlers and championship, tournament and elimination options.

games.title: Super Fire Pro Wrestling
games.significance: Fire Pro's first major Super Famicom milestone.
games.history: The series moved into the 16-bit Super Famicom era with a bigger presentation and an evolving roster.

games.title: Super Fire Pro Wrestling 2
games.significance: A bridge between the original Super game and Final Bout.
games.history: A follow-up to the first Super Famicom entry, continuing the series' rapid 16-bit development.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling 3: Legend Bout
games.significance: One of the final original PC Engine milestones.
games.history: The PC Engine branch grew to 32 challengers, including singles, tag and handicap exhibition matches.

games.title: Super Fire Pro Wrestling III: Final Bout
games.significance: A pivotal step for the expanding wrestler roster and Edit feature.
games.history: A larger 16-bit entry notable for its 64 playable wrestlers, wrestler editing and new battle royal options.

games.title: Super Fire Pro Wrestling Special
games.significance: A distinctive story-mode experiment in the 16-bit series.
games.history: A Super Famicom entry remembered for its unusual story campaign and further refinement of the Fire Pro formula.

screenshots.title: Super Fire Pro Wrestling Special — ring action
Super Fire Pro Wrestling Special — Gruesome Fighting

games.title: Super Fire Pro Wrestling X
games.significance: A major late-generation 16-bit milestone, followed by X Premium in March 1996.
games.history: Released in Japan on December 22, 1995 by Human Entertainment, Super Fire Pro Wrestling X brought one of the most ambitious sprite-based wrestling rosters to the Super Famicom. Its timed grapples and wide range of Japanese and American wrestling styles were complemented by tournaments, leagues, championship pursuits, four-person battle royals and wrestler editing. It also brought characters from the Blazing Tornado arcade branch into the main Fire Pro world.
games.features: Play singles, tag matches, one-night dream matches, leagues, elimination contests and a four-wrestler battle royal. Edit mode lets you create wrestlers with individual moves, appearance and skills.
alternateTitles: Super Fire Pro Wrestling X Premium

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling Iron Slam '96
games.significance: An experimental 3D branch of the Fire Pro family.
games.history: An early polygonal experiment on PlayStation, quite different visually from Fire Pro's familiar sprites.
games.noBoxArtReason: LaunchBox only has a logo on white (no box scan)

games.title: Fire Prowrestling S: 6Men Scramble
games.significance: A memorable multi-person Saturn outing.
games.history: Six wrestlers could appear at once in the Saturn installment, alongside six-man tags and a large roster.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling G
games.significance: A late-1990s console milestone discussed in the official World developer retrospective.
games.history: The PlayStation title occupies an important point between Human-era Fire Pro and the Spike-produced games.
games.features: Late PlayStation-era Fire Pro; connects the 16-bit era to the Dreamcast and PS2 period.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling
games.significance: The handheld entry that introduced Fire Pro to many players outside Japan.
games.history: The WonderSwan version began in 2000; a Game Boy Advance edition became Fire Pro's first official North American release in 2001.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling D
games.significance: A substantial Dreamcast home for Fire Pro creation.
games.history: The Dreamcast installment extended the classic presentation and edit tools to wrestlers, referees, organizations and rings.
games.features: Includes wrestler, referee, ring and organization editing in the Dreamcast entry.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling 2
games.significance: Continues Fire Pro's portable international expansion.
games.history: The second officially English-language Game Boy Advance release followed the first handheld Fire Pro.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling Z
games.significance: One of the last major entries before Returns.
games.history: A PlayStation 2 entry with a large move library and a team-centered story/career-style campaign.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling Returns
games.significance: The final mainline Fire Pro before its modern revival.
games.history: The classic sprite-based series returned on PlayStation 2 before a long gap leading to World.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling (Xbox Live Arcade)
games.significance: A separate avatar-wrestling experiment, distinct from the traditional sprite games.
games.history: An unusual Xbox Live Avatar-based take on Fire Pro with online and offline matches.

games.title: Fire Pro Wrestling World
games.significance: A new generation of edits, Workshop sharing and modern Fire Pro.
games.history: World revived Fire Pro on Steam in 2017 and PlayStation 4 in 2018, restoring deep wrestler and ring customization.

games.title: King of Colosseum Red
games.significance: Its wrestlers can be carried into Green and combined for a much larger roster.
games.history: The Red disc focuses on New Japan, All Japan and Pancrase, and features 96 characters alongside a trial-mode progression system.
games.features: Trial mode has season-like progression and unlockable wrestlers, rings and championships. The Red disc emphasizes NJPW, AJPW and Pancrase.

videos.title: King of Colosseum Red footage (series retrospective, Red segment)

games.title: King of Colosseum Green
games.significance: A complementary companion disc that expands the promotions and gameplay options of Red.
games.history: The Green disc centers on NOAH and Zero-One and adds 58 wrestlers; combined Red/Green save content can reach 154 characters.
games.features: NOAH and Zero-One headline this disc. Its Trial mode unlocks more wrestlers, edits, championships and other content.

videos.title: King of Colosseum Green footage (series retrospective, Green segment)

games.title: King of Colosseum II
games.significance: The single-disc sequel expands the roster and adds a dedicated Match Maker booking mode.
games.history: The later sequel brings the Japanese wrestling simulation branch together in one PlayStation 2 game, with more than 160 licensed wrestlers.
games.features: Match Maker lets players book promotion matches. Exhibition, Survival Road, Title Match, Series, Edit and Dojo modes offer additional career and match options.

games.title: Fire Pro Joshi: All-Star Dream Slam
games.significance: A full joshi-focused sibling rather than a reskin of the main Fire Pro roster.
games.history: Released July 22, 1994, this women's wrestling entry focuses on the stars and rivalries of Japan's joshi promotions. It takes Fire Pro's deliberate grappling rhythm into a dedicated all-women roster rather than treating women's wrestling as a small addition to the main game.

games.title: Fire Pro Gaiden: Blazing Tornado
games.significance: The arcade cousin of Fire Pro—and a bridge to Super Fire Pro Wrestling X.
games.history: The faster, more arcade-oriented branch of Human Entertainment's wrestling family debuted in arcades on August 25, 1994, with distinctive fictional wrestlers and a more colorful presentation. Several of its wrestlers later appeared as recognizable crossovers in Fire Pro Wrestling X.

games.title: Super Fire Pro Wrestling: Queen's Special
games.significance: A distinctly women-focused late-16-bit entry from the creators of Fire Pro.
games.history: Released June 30, 1995, Queen's Special expanded Human's focus on Japanese women's professional wrestling. Its separate joshi-centered identity makes it an important part of the Fire Pro family alongside the better-known mixed and men's rosters.

games.noBoxArtReason: LaunchBox only has a logo card (no box scan)
